name: Del Haskins
lines: *Del's rig pulls in, headlights cutting through the fog.
There they are! Survived your first night. Most don't make it to the second, y'know. Quit, I mean. Ha.
Coffee, if you would.

inspect.label: Face
inspect.text: Same old Del. A little more tired. He keeps rubbing his eyes.

inspect.label: Reflection
inspect.text: Normal.

reply: Worst on the reservoir curve. I swear I saw a little kid in a yellow raincoat on the shoulder back there.
Stopped and looked. Nobody. Gave me the creeps.
You remembered! See, this is why I like you. Mara used to do that.

lines: Two nights running. You're a pro. Here — for luck.
*He slides a battered keychain across the counter: a little plastic bus with 313 on the side.
Found it in the parking lot years back. Never felt right keeping it.
That's the stuff. See you tomorrow, kid.
Ah, come on. Fine. Tomorrow.

name: The Passenger
lines: *A man in a brown 1980s suit and a fogged pair of glasses steps up, briefcase in hand. His cuffs are damp.
Evening. Is the 2:58 running late, do you know? I've been waiting at that stop for... well. A while.
Coffee, please. Black. It's going to be a long trip to Holloway.
payment: Two dollar bills and two quarters. The bills are 1985 series.

inspect.label: Face
inspect.text: Polite, harried, mid-forties. His glasses are fogged on the inside, and they never clear.

inspect.label: Ticket
inspect.text:
A ticket sticks out of his breast pocket.
MERIDIAN COACH LINES — COACH 313 — 10/13/87 — DEP 2:58 AM.

inspect.label: Reflection
inspect.text: His reflection is there. Its suit is darker — soaked through.

inspect.label: SCAN
inspect.text: PULSE: NONE.  TEMP 10°C.  RESIDUE: HIGH.  DISPOSITION: WAITING.

cameras.note: On CAM 1, the bus stop sign behind him reads 2:58 in faint white numbers.

talk.text: There's no bus that stops here anymore.
reply: Ha! That's what they said last time, too. There's always a bus.
Ellis Crane. Mutual Hearth Insurance. I've got a meeting in Holloway at nine.
Crane. Ellis Crane. Pleasure.
You know, you look a little like my daughter. She'd be — oh, she'd be about your age by now. Isn't that a funny thing to say?

lines: Ah. Wonderful. Thank you.
*He takes it back to the bus stop and stands under the sign, sipping, watching the road for headlights.
Oh — that's not coffee. Never mind, never mind. I'll manage.
No coffee? That's all right. I'll wait. I'm very good at waiting.

name: Night Runner
lines: *A woman in a reflective running vest jogs in place at the machine, breath steaming.
Water. Please. Fog's so thick I nearly ran into the lake.
payment: A card that taps. The reader beeps green.

inspect.label: Face
inspect.text: Flushed, breathing hard, very alive.

inspect.label: Reflection
inspect.text: Her reflection jogs in place with her, step for step.

inspect.label: SCAN
inspect.text: PULSE 148  TEMP 37.4°C  RESIDUE: NONE

reply: Some guy in a suit at the bus stop. Briefcase and everything. In this fog? Weird.
Also, there's a puddle by the trail that doesn't reflect anything. I'm not running past it again.

lines: Bless you. Okay. Two more miles. Don't let anybody tell you running at midnight is crazy.
Uh. I said water. That's fine, I'll find a fountain.
Seriously? Okay. Bye.

name: The Collector
lines: *He is very tall. His coat is pinstriped, his gloves are gray, and you never quite see his face under the brim of his hat. He carries a ledger.
Good evening. You must be the new attendant. How very nice.
I'm not here for anything on your menu. I'd like whatever the machine made on its own last night. The can without a label.
I'll pay well. Twenty dollars.
payment: A crisp twenty-dollar bill. The serial number is all zeros.

inspect.label: Face
inspect.text: You look for his face. Your eyes keep sliding to the ledger instead, as if they've been told not to.

inspect.label: Ledger
inspect.text: A thick black ledger, columns of names in fine handwriting. He closes it before you can read any.

inspect.label: Reflection
inspect.text: In the glass, there is a tall shape. It is not wearing a coat. It is not wearing anything you have a word for.

inspect.label: SCAN
inspect.text: ERROR. ERROR. SUBJECT OUTSIDE CALIBRATION RANGE.

cameras.note: CAM 1 shows him, very tall, very still.
CAM 2: no one at the unit. The glass is fogging, as if someone is breathing on it.

reply: A client of your employer. A very old one. They'll tell you I'm a valued partner.
I collect things. Change, mostly.

talk.text: Why do you want the can?
reply: Because the machine made it, and what the machine makes is mine by contract. Clause four.
But I like to pay. It keeps things friendly.
And I remember you. You're one of my best customers.
Round and round we go. The minute never closes. Not really.

lines: *He takes the warm can in his gray glove and it goes quiet, the way a room goes quiet when someone stops crying.
Thank you. You and I are going to get along.
*He writes something in the ledger. You hear your own name in the scratching of the pen.
That's not what I asked for. But how sweet of you.
*He leaves the item on the counter untouched. It has gone cold, though it came out warm.
Polite. I appreciate polite.
*He tips his hat. He is gone before you see him walk away.

name: The Silent Child
lines: *A small girl in a yellow raincoat stands on tiptoe at the glass. She doesn't say anything.
*She presses a toy against the window: a little yellow bus. Then she taps the gum slot, B4, three times.
*She waits, looking up at you.
payment: She has no money. She places a crayon drawing face-down on the tray instead.

inspect.label: Face
inspect.text: Pale, freckled, about seven. Her hair is wet at the ends. She looks scared — but not of you.

inspect.label: Raincoat
inspect.text: Her raincoat is dry. Her shoes are soaked, and there is weed tangled in the laces.

inspect.label: Reflection
inspect.text: Her reflection matches her. It holds up the toy bus too.

inspect.label: Drawing
inspect.text: A crayon drawing: a yellow bus upside down in blue water. On the shore, a woman with a mouth that goes all the way across her face.

inspect.label: SCAN
inspect.text: PULSE: NONE.  TEMP 8°C.  RESIDUE: HIGH.  DISPOSITION: FRIGHTENED.

cameras.note: Not on CAM 2. On CAM 1 she keeps looking over her shoulder at the bus stop.

reply: *She shakes her head. She points to the bus stop. Then to the reservoir. Then to the machine.
*She goes very still. She points at the drawing, at the woman with the huge mouth, and shakes her head hard. No. No.

lines: *She unwraps the gum with careful fingers and chews, eyes closed, like it's the best thing in the world.
*She leaves the drawing on the tray and runs off toward the trees.
*She looks at it, puzzled, then takes it anyway and holds it to her chest. She leaves the drawing.
*She nods like she understands, leaves the drawing on the tray, and walks away into the fog without looking back.

name: The Passenger
lines: *Mr. Crane comes back to the machine. He is soaking wet now, head to toe. Water drips from his briefcase.
I'm sorry — this is going to sound strange.
The bus came. I got on. And then there was water everywhere, and then I was standing at the stop again.
Why do I keep getting off here? What... what's the date today?

inspect.label: Face
inspect.text: Terrified, trying very hard to be reasonable about it.

inspect.label: Reflection
inspect.text: His reflection is underwater. Bubbles rise from its mouth when he talks.

talk.text: Tell him the truth: it's 2026. The bus crashed in 1987.
"The next bus will be along soon."

lines: *He stares at you. For a long time he doesn't say anything.
...Twenty-twenty-six.
I think I knew. I think I've known for a very long time.
Thank you. Nobody's ever told me. Every time, they just give me coffee.
*He walks back to the bus stop and sits on the curb. He doesn't watch the road anymore.
*He breathes out, relieved.
Of course. Of course. Silly of me.
*He goes back to the stop and watches the road, and does not see the water rising around his shoes.
*He takes the coffee and doesn't drink it.
Coffee. Yes. That's what they always give me.
*He goes back to the stop.
*He waits for an answer that doesn't come, then walks back to the stop.

name: The Smiling Woman
lines: *Mrs. Marsh is back. Her curls are perfect. Her smile has gotten wider since last night. Not by much.
Hello again, dear! Have you seen my daughter tonight?
Yellow raincoat. Loves strawberry gum. She came by, didn't she? I can smell it.

inspect.label: Face
inspect.text: Her smile shows more teeth than last night. Her eyes do not join in.

inspect.label: Reflection
inspect.text: Her reflection is not smiling. It is standing behind the machine, looking for something.

inspect.label: SCAN
inspect.text: PULSE: NONE.  RESIDUE: ABNORMAL.  NOTE: SUBJECT PRESENT AT TWO LOCATIONS.

cameras.note: CAM 3 (stockroom): a woman in a 1980s coat is standing among the boxes with her back to the camera.

talk.text: "She was here earlier. She went toward the trees."
reply: *The smile widens by a fraction of an inch.
Thank you. Thank you so much. I'll find her now.
Hm. You'd tell me. Wouldn't you, dear?

lines: Lovely. She'll come for this.
*She walks off toward the trees, humming a lullaby in the wrong key.
No, no. Never mind.
*She leaves, humming.
*Her smile stays exactly the same. Her voice doesn't.
Another time.
